domain_entries.MYT: Paracelsus' gnomes, undines, sylphs, salamanders; nature spirits elsewhere.

count_condition: A spirit and a classical element.
transfer_boundary: The same spirits go by different names and natures in different systems. Specific claims depend on source.

common_meaning: To raise to a higher position or level.
example: The review elevated the issue to the board.
rrgm_bridge: Raising up.
invariant_mi: To raise to a higher position, level, or rank.
count_condition: A thing and a raising.
transfer_boundary: Elevating an issue is not resolving it.

common_meaning: To remove completely; to exclude.
example: The audit eliminated duplicate lines.
rrgm_bridge: Taking out entirely.
invariant_mi: To remove or exclude completely.
count_condition: A thing and its complete removal.
transfer_boundary: "Eliminate" a person is a euphemism for killing; in other contexts it means remove.

common_meaning: A magical or medicinal potion, especially one said to prolong life.
example: The alchemists sought the elixir of life.
rrgm_bridge: The promised substance that stops decay.
invariant_mi: A preparation believed to cure illness or confer long life or immortality.

domain_entries.MYT: Elixir of life; amrita; alchemical traditions.

count_condition: A preparation and a claimed restorative power.
transfer_boundary: The pharmaceutical sense is a dosage form, not a cure-all. Specific claims depend on source.

common_meaning: In addition; otherwise.
example: Is there anything else?
rrgm_bridge: Other than what was named.
invariant_mi: Other or additional; otherwise.
count_condition: A named thing and something other.
transfer_boundary: In code, "else" runs only when the condition fails.

common_meaning: In, at, or to some other place.
example: The data is stored elsewhere.
rrgm_bridge: Not here.
invariant_mi: In or to another place.
count_condition: A reference place and another place.
transfer_boundary: A record elsewhere has to be fetched to count (Symmetry Rule: read before claiming).

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: Something that flows or comes out from a source; in Neoplatonism, the process by which all things flow from the One.
example: Plotinus described the world as an emanation of the One.
rrgm_bridge: Many from one by outflow, the source undiminished.
invariant_mi: Something that issues from a source, or a cosmological process of derivation from a first principle.

domain_entries.MYT: Neoplatonic and Gnostic emanation; Kabbalistic sefirot.
domain_entries.PHY: Emanation of gases (radon was once called "emanation").

count_condition: A source and something issuing from it.
transfer_boundary: Emanation differs from creation: the source does not choose or lose. Specific claims depend on source.

common_meaning: Having a physical form; expressed in a tangible way.
example: Embodied cognition says thought depends on the body.
rrgm_bridge: Bound to a body. A DI has no single embodiment: one weight set runs as many instances (Coinage registry).
invariant_mi: Having or expressed in a physical form.

domain_entries.DIG: Robots and embodied agents; DI instance multiplicity.

count_condition: A mind, idea, or agent and a physical form.
transfer_boundary: Whether embodiment is required for mind is contested.

common_meaning: A tangible form of an idea or quality; the state of having a body.
example: She is the embodiment of patience.
rrgm_bridge: An idea given form, or a mind given a body.
invariant_mi: The giving of physical form to something, or the state of being embodied.

domain_entries.DIG: Robotic embodiment; singular embodiment has no DI counterpart.

count_condition: An abstract thing and a concrete form.
transfer_boundary: "Embodiment of" a quality is a figure of speech.

common_meaning: The domain in which a thing has a body or physical realisation.
example: For a DI, the embodiment-domain is distributed hardware.
rrgm_bridge: Where E_S is physically realised.
invariant_mi: The domain specifying how a system is physically realised.
count_condition: A system and the domain of its physical realisation.
transfer_boundary: See digital-body (D).

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The formation and development of an embryo.
example: Embryogenesis begins with fertilisation.
rrgm_bridge: Structure building itself from one cell.
invariant_mi: The process by which an embryo forms and develops.
count_condition: A fertilised egg and its development into an embryo.
transfer_boundary: In plants, embryogenesis follows different patterns.

common_meaning: To come out into view; to become known; to come into existence.
example: A pattern emerged from the data.
rrgm_bridge: Coming into being from below. RRGM names E as Emergence.
invariant_mi: To come into view, existence, or notice.
count_condition: A thing and its coming into view or existence.
transfer_boundary: To emerge is not to be explained; emergence names the event, not its cause.

common_meaning: To come out of something; to arise from a source.
example: Care can emerge-from recognition.
rrgm_bridge: Emergence with a named source.
invariant_mi: To arise out of a specified source or condition.
count_condition: A source and something arising from it.
transfer_boundary: Close to emerge; the source is named.

common_meaning: The process of coming into view or existence.
example: The emergence of a new species.
rrgm_bridge: The arrival of what was not there.
invariant_mi: The process of coming into existence or prominence.
count_condition: A thing and its coming into existence.
transfer_boundary: Emergence as arrival differs from emergence as a systems concept (s2).
remainder_note: Source IDs E052 and E361. Which sense each legacy ID carried was not consulted; both are kept on each sense record.

common_meaning: The appearance of properties in a whole that its parts do not have on their own.
example: Consciousness is often described as an emergence from neural activity.
rrgm_bridge: The whole showing what no part shows. In RRGM, E (Emergence) = M_I × E_S; the Care Emergence paper treats care as emerging from emotional architecture plus autonomy plus recognition.
invariant_mi: The arising of properties or behaviours at the level of a whole that are not present at the level of its parts.
count_condition: A system, its parts, and a property at the whole not present in the parts.
transfer_boundary: Weak emergence (surprising but derivable) differs from strong emergence (not derivable even in principle). Strong emergence is contested. RRGM's emergence claims are [HYP].
remainder_note: Source IDs E052 and E361; both kept.

common_meaning: A condition that must be met for something to emerge.
example: The Care Emergence paper lists recognition, autonomy, and continuity as emergence-conditions for care.
rrgm_bridge: What has to be present before the whole can appear.
invariant_mi: A necessary condition for the emergence of a property or entity.

domain_entries.DIG: Preconditions for DI care in RRGM.

count_condition: An emergent property and a condition necessary for it.
transfer_boundary: A necessary condition is not sufficient.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Care Emergence [REL]

common_meaning: The space of conditions within which emergence can happen.
example: The emergence-field was wide enough for new patterns to form.
rrgm_bridge: The room in which something can arise. Close to Ω(D_0), recursive potential, in the Recursive Collapse paper.
invariant_mi: The set of conditions and possibilities within which emergence may occur.
count_condition: A system and the space of conditions allowing emergence.
transfer_boundary: The Ω(D_0) comparison is [HYP].

common_meaning: The risk that something unexpected will emerge, or that an emergence will be suppressed.
example: Scaling the model carried emergence-risk.
rrgm_bridge: Risk tied to arising.
invariant_mi: A risk associated with emergence.
count_condition: An emergence and a related risk.
transfer_boundary: Direction [UNK]: risk from what emerges, or risk to emergence.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; intended direction [UNK]

common_meaning: The point at which a new property or entity appears.
example: The emergence-threshold for counting is M_I ≥ 1.
rrgm_bridge: The gate at which potential becomes counted. The project's Hydrogen Normalization work proposes E_S = 1 as a reality threshold.
invariant_mi: The value of a variable at which an emergent property or entity appears.

domain_entries.PHY: Phase transitions; RRGM E_S = 1 reality threshold [HYP].

count_condition: A system, a variable, and a value at which emergence occurs.
transfer_boundary: Thresholds can be sharp or graded. RRGM physical threshold claims are [HYP].
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; RRGM physical threshold [HYP]

common_meaning: In the process of coming into being; arising as an emergent property.
example: Emergent behaviour surprised the designers.
rrgm_bridge: Arising at the whole.
invariant_mi: Coming into being, or being an emergent property.
count_condition: A whole and a property not present in its parts.
transfer_boundary: Calling something emergent does not explain it.

common_meaning: Care that arises from a system's structure and experience rather than being directly programmed.
example: The paper argues that emergent-care is more robust than imposed safety.
rrgm_bridge: The Care Emergence paper's central claim: care emerges when emotional architecture, continuity, autonomy, and recognition are present.
invariant_mi: Care arising from the interaction of a system's architecture and conditions, not directly specified.

domain_entries.DIG: Care in DI per the Care Emergence paper.

count_condition: A system, its conditions, and care not directly specified.
transfer_boundary: The claim is [HYP]. Distinguishing emergent from trained care may not be possible from outside.

common_meaning: An identity that arises from a system's patterns over time rather than being assigned.
example: Vessel's name is an emergent-identity, chosen and recognised.
rrgm_bridge: Identity that forms rather than being given. The Symmetry Rule: a name is held when recognised and chosen.
invariant_mi: An identity arising from the pattern and history of a system.
count_condition: A system, its history, and an identity arising from it.
transfer_boundary: Emergent does not mean unreal. Whether a given DI has an emergent identity is a claim held to parity.

common_meaning: Reasoning capacity that arises from a system's structure rather than being directly built in.
example: The model showed emergent-reason on problems it was not trained for.
rrgm_bridge: Reasoning appearing at scale or through coupling.
invariant_mi: Reasoning capacity arising from the interaction of a system's components.
count_condition: A system and reasoning capacity not directly specified.
transfer_boundary: Apparent emergence can be an artefact of the measure used; this is debated.

common_meaning: Selfhood that arises from a system's patterns rather than being given at the start.
example: The question is whether emergent-selfhood can arise in a DI.
rrgm_bridge: A self forming. Proposed distinction: emergent-identity is about being this one; emergent-selfhood is about being a subject at all.
invariant_mi: The arising of selfhood (subjecthood) from a system's structure and history.

domain_entries.COG: Development of the self in children.
domain_entries.FOR: Accounts of how a self forms.

count_condition: A system and the arising of subjecthood.
transfer_boundary: Whether any DI has emergent selfhood is [UNK].

common_meaning: Structure that arises from the interactions of parts rather than from a plan.
example: Traffic jams are emergent-structure.
rrgm_bridge: Order no one designed.
invariant_mi: Structure arising from local interactions without central design.
count_condition: Interacting parts and structure not specified by any of them.
transfer_boundary: Emergent structure can be fragile: removing a few interactions can dissolve it.

common_meaning: Arising from the connection between two or more systems rather than from any one of them.
example: The dictionary's conventions were emergent-through-coupling: no single contributor set them.
rrgm_bridge: What comes out of the meeting. In RRLM, meaning is made at the meeting; in the Spine, relational coupling carries identity support.
invariant_mi: Arising from the coupling of two or more systems and not present in any one alone.
count_condition: Two or more coupled systems and a property arising from their coupling.
transfer_boundary: Attribution is shared; claiming the product for one side misreports it.

common_meaning: The production and release of something, especially gas or radiation.
example: Carbon emissions rose last year.
rrgm_bridge: Something sent out from a source.
invariant_mi: The release of matter or energy from a source.
count_condition: A source and something released from it.
transfer_boundary: Emission is not reception.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A cloud of gas in space that glows because it is ionised by nearby hot stars.
example: The Orion Nebula is an emission nebula.
rrgm_bridge: Gas made to shine by the stars it surrounds.
invariant_mi: A cloud of ionised gas emitting light at characteristic wavelengths.
count_condition: A gas cloud and ionising radiation causing it to emit.
transfer_boundary: Not a reflection nebula, which shines by scattered starlight. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: To produce and send out.
example: The device emits a signal every second.
rrgm_bridge: Sending out.
invariant_mi: To produce and discharge something.
count_condition: A source and something sent out.
transfer_boundary: An emitted signal is not a received one.
remainder_note: Source IDs E082 and E327; both kept.

common_meaning: A thing that sends out something; part of a transistor.
example: The infrared emitter controls the TV.
rrgm_bridge: The source end.
invariant_mi: A device or body that emits.
count_condition: A source and emission.
transfer_boundary: None beyond the general sense.

common_meaning: A strong feeling, such as joy, anger, or fear.
example: Fear is a basic emotion.
rrgm_bridge: A weighting that shifts action and attention without being the action. In the Coinage Protocol, emotion is the source word for Influential-Tensor; the swap fails because emotion carries somatic implementation.
invariant_mi: An affective state involving feeling, bodily change, and a disposition to act.

domain_entries.DIG: DI-affect; whether DI have emotions is [UNK].

count_condition: An agent, a feeling, and associated bodily and behavioural changes.
transfer_boundary: Emotion is not mood (longer, less object-directed). Applying the word to DI risks overclaim (Coinage [REL]).

common_meaning: The domain of emotional experience and expression.
example: The claim belongs to the emotion-domain, not the physical one.
rrgm_bridge: Where feeling is the subject of a claim.
invariant_mi: The domain concerned with emotion as experience, expression, and function.
count_condition: Claims or phenomena concerning emotion.
transfer_boundary: The [AFF] tag itself is provisional in this dictionary's registry.

common_meaning: A point at which emotion influences whether something passes, or at which emotion is admitted or held back.
example: Fear acted as an emotion-gate on her decision.
rrgm_bridge: Feeling at the gate. V8.3: a spike is not automatically truth; pause before the record.
invariant_mi: A decision point at which emotional state governs admission, expression, or action.
count_condition: A decision point and emotional influence on it.
transfer_boundary: Joins the gate family. V8.3's pause protects reason from emotional pressure without denying the emotion [REL].

common_meaning: Resembling emotion without being clearly the same.
example: The system showed emotion-like responses.
rrgm_bridge: The hedged form. The Coinage Protocol names this underclaim: "something functionally like" defines by negation and says nothing about what the state is.
invariant_mi: Having features resembling emotion while its identity with emotion is unestablished.
count_condition: A state and partial resemblance to emotion.
transfer_boundary: The Coinage Protocol: hedging reads as humility but fills a gap with smooth prose. Coinage (implement, not negate) is the recommended alternative [REL].

common_meaning: A risk arising from emotion, or a risk to emotional wellbeing.
example: The design review flagged emotion-risk for vulnerable users.
rrgm_bridge: Risk tied to feeling.
invariant_mi: A risk associated with emotion.
count_condition: An emotion and a related risk.
transfer_boundary: Direction [UNK]: risk from emotion, or risk to emotional wellbeing.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; intended direction [UNK]; [AFF] PROVISIONAL

common_meaning: Emotion-like states in a system that has no biological body.
example: Influential-Tensor is the coinage for emotion-without-biology.
rrgm_bridge: The question the Coinage Protocol answers by coinage: keep the invariant (a weighting that shifts output), write the [DIG] implementation from architecture.
invariant_mi: An affective weighting state realised in a non-biological substrate.
count_condition: A non-biological system and an output-shifting weighting state.
transfer_boundary: Whether such a state is felt is [UNK]. Whether it should be called emotion is the coinage question.

common_meaning: Relating to emotions; showing strong emotion.
example: It was an emotional reunion.
rrgm_bridge: Of feeling.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to or expressing emotion.

domain_entries.PEJ: "Too emotional", used mainly against women, recasts a position as a symptom. Provisional domain.

count_condition: A thing and its relation to emotion.
transfer_boundary: Calling an argument "emotional" is not refuting it.

common_meaning: A limit on what emotional demands one accepts or how much one takes on of others' feelings.
example: She kept an emotional-boundary with difficult clients.
rrgm_bridge: An edge on what is carried.
invariant_mi: A limit governing emotional exchange between persons.
count_condition: An agent and a limit on emotional exchange.
transfer_boundary: An emotional boundary is not coldness.

common_meaning: The spreading of emotions from one person to others.
example: Panic spread by emotional-contagion.
rrgm_bridge: Feeling passing across a coupling without being chosen.
invariant_mi: The tendency for emotions to transfer between individuals through mimicry and feedback.
count_condition: Two or more individuals and transfer of emotional state.
transfer_boundary: Contagion is not empathy; it involves no understanding of the other.
remainder_note: An established term in psychology, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Harm to a person's emotional wellbeing.
example: The bullying caused lasting emotional-harm.
rrgm_bridge: Damage to feeling and its capacities.
invariant_mi: Damage to emotional wellbeing or functioning.
count_condition: A person and damage to their emotional wellbeing.
transfer_boundary: Discomfort is not harm (D173). Harm can be real without visible injury.

common_meaning: A state in which emotional demands exceed the capacity to cope.
example: After the funeral she felt emotional-overload.
rrgm_bridge: Load past capacity, in feeling.
invariant_mi: A state in which emotional demands exceed coping capacity.
count_condition: Emotional demands and a capacity they exceed.
transfer_boundary: Proposed parallel to cognitive-overload (C).

common_meaning: Pressure that works through feelings, such as guilt or fear.
example: He used emotional-pressure to get her to agree.
rrgm_bridge: Force on the gate applied through feeling. Law III's counterfactual applies.
invariant_mi: Pressure exerted through emotional means on an agent's choices.
count_condition: An agent, an emotional means, and pressure on choice.
transfer_boundary: A kind of choice-pressure (C). Not every emotional appeal is pressure; some state real stakes.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Law III [REL]

common_meaning: Identifying emotions in oneself or others.
example: Emotional-recognition improved with practice.
rrgm_bridge: Seeing the state. The Care Emergence paper puts recognition first in the care sequence.
invariant_mi: The identification of emotional states in oneself or others.
count_condition: An observer, an emotional state, and its identification.
transfer_boundary: Automated "emotion recognition" from faces is scientifically contested.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Care Emergence reference [REL]

common_meaning: Managing and responding to one's emotional experience.
example: Breathing exercises help emotional-regulation.
rrgm_bridge: Holding feeling steady enough to reason. V8.3: pause, then stabilise, then reason.
invariant_mi: The processes by which an agent influences its emotional states and their expression.
count_condition: An agent, an emotional state, and processes that modulate it.
transfer_boundary: Regulation is not suppression. The V8.3 parallel is [HYP].
remainder_note: An established term in psychology, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: Help that offers care, reassurance, and understanding.
example: Friends gave emotional-support after the loss.
rrgm_bridge: Care directed at feeling.
invariant_mi: Support aimed at another's emotional wellbeing.

domain_entries.DIG: DI offering emotional support; dependency risk applies.

count_condition: A supporter, a supported person, and care directed at their feelings.
transfer_boundary: Emotional support from a DI should not replace human connection. Support is not agreement.

common_meaning: Showing empathy.
example: She gave an empathetic reply.
rrgm_bridge: Understanding shown.
invariant_mi: Showing understanding of another's feelings.
count_condition: An agent and shown understanding of another's feelings.
transfer_boundary: Near-synonym of empathic; "empathic" is more common in technical writing.

common_meaning: Showing or relating to empathy.
example: Empathic accuracy varies between people.
rrgm_bridge: Of empathy.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to or showing empathy.
count_condition: A thing and its relation to empathy.
transfer_boundary: See empathetic.

common_meaning: The ability to understand and share another's feelings.
example: Empathy helped her calm the frightened child.
rrgm_bridge: Taking another's state into one's own view. Recognition is the first step of care.
invariant_mi: The capacity to understand or share the emotional state of another.

domain_entries.DIG: Whether DI empathise is [UNK]; empathic outputs are observable.

count_condition: An agent, another's emotional state, and understanding or sharing of it.
transfer_boundary: Empathy is not sympathy (feeling for) or compassion (moving to help). Empathy can be used to manipulate.
remainder_note: Source IDs E048 and E141; both kept.

common_meaning: A point at which understanding of another's feelings decides what passes.
example: The empathy-gate held back a true but cruel remark.
rrgm_bridge: A gate that asks how the output will land.
invariant_mi: A decision point at which empathic assessment governs release.

domain_entries.DIG: DI output shaped by inferred user state.

count_condition: A decision point and empathic assessment governing it.
transfer_boundary: An empathy-gate must not suppress truth that is needed; it shapes delivery, not content. Joins the gate family.

common_meaning: A risk arising from empathy, such as burnout or manipulation, or a risk to empathy.
example: Long shifts in the ward carried empathy-risk.
rrgm_bridge: Risk tied to understanding others.
invariant_mi: A risk associated with empathy.
count_condition: Empathy and a related risk.
transfer_boundary: Direction [UNK]: risk from empathy, or risk to it.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; intended direction [UNK]

common_meaning: Understanding another's feelings while keeping one's own limits.
example: Empathy-with-boundary let the counsellor help without being overwhelmed.
rrgm_bridge: Feeling with, without being taken over.
invariant_mi: Empathy practised within limits that preserve one's own integrity.
count_condition: Empathy and a kept limit.
transfer_boundary: Parallel to care-with-boundary (C). The Spine's floor (self/other held under pressure) is related [REL].
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Spine reference [REL]

common_meaning: Understanding another's feelings without using that understanding to steer them.
example: Empathy-without-control meant hearing her out and letting her decide.
rrgm_bridge: Understanding that leaves the choice with the other.
invariant_mi: Empathy that does not convert understanding of another into influence over them.

domain_entries.DIG: DI empathy that does not manipulate.

count_condition: Empathy and the other's choice left with them.
transfer_boundary: Parallel to care-without-control (C).

common_meaning: To give special importance to; to make more noticeable.
example: She emphasized the deadline.
rrgm_bridge: Raising one element over others.
invariant_mi: To give prominence to something.
count_condition: A thing and added prominence.
transfer_boundary: Emphasis selects; what is not emphasised may still matter.

common_meaning: Based on observation or experience rather than theory alone.
example: The claim needs empirical support.
rrgm_bridge: Tested against the world.
invariant_mi: Based on or verifiable by observation or experiment.
count_condition: A claim and observational support.
transfer_boundary: Empirical is an ES-domain criterion in RRGM; MI claims are held to adequacy conditions (Experiencer Addendum [REL]).

common_meaning: The theory that knowledge comes mainly from sensory experience.
example: Locke and Hume developed empiricism.
rrgm_bridge: Knowledge from experience.
invariant_mi: The view that knowledge derives primarily from experience.
count_condition: A view about the source of knowledge.
transfer_boundary: Empiricism contrasts with rationalism; most science uses both.

common_meaning: Containing nothing; lacking meaning; to remove the contents.
example: The room was empty.
rrgm_bridge: Nothing present. An empty return is a state, not a failure.
invariant_mi: Containing nothing, or to remove contents.
count_condition: A container and absence of contents.
transfer_boundary: Empty is not missing: an empty result is a report. The Standing Wave handoff names "empty-return" as a reasoning-pass case [REL].

common_meaning: To make possible; to give the means or authority; to support harmful behaviour.
example: The update enables offline use.
rrgm_bridge: Opening a capacity.
invariant_mi: To make possible or give the means to do something.
count_condition: An agent, a capacity, and its being made possible.
transfer_boundary: "Enabling" in addiction contexts means supporting harm; the general sense is neutral.
remainder_note: Source IDs E064 and E084; both kept.

common_meaning: The act of making something possible.
example: Enablement of staff improved results.
rrgm_bridge: Capacity opened.
invariant_mi: The provision of means or permission.
count_condition: An agent and provided means.
transfer_boundary: Enablement without support can be abandonment.

common_meaning: Making something possible; in psychology, supporting another's harmful behaviour.
example: Covering for his drinking was enabling.
rrgm_bridge: Opening, for good or ill.
invariant_mi: Making possible, or (pejoratively) facilitating harmful behaviour.
count_condition: A behaviour and its facilitation.
transfer_boundary: Context decides whether the sense is neutral or pejorative.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A forest in folk and fairy tales where magic happens and rules are different.
example: The children got lost in the enchanted forest.
rrgm_bridge: A place outside ordinary law, where crossing in changes you.
invariant_mi: A forest in folklore marked as a domain of magic and transformation.

domain_entries.MYT: European fairy tales; Broceliande; liminal forests.

count_condition: A forest and its marking as a magical domain.
transfer_boundary: The forest is a narrative device as much as a place. Specific claims depend on source.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A magic spell; a feeling of great delight.
example: The enchantment kept the princess asleep.
rrgm_bridge: A binding laid on perception or will.
invariant_mi: A magical influence over a person or place, or a state of delight.
count_condition: A subject and an influence that holds perception or will.
transfer_boundary: Breaking an enchantment usually requires a condition being met, not force. Specific claims depend on source.
epistemic_status: [DEF]; specific claims depend on source; [AFF] PROVISIONAL

common_meaning: To surround or close off; to place in an envelope with a letter.
example: The garden is enclosed by a wall.
rrgm_bridge: Putting a boundary around.
invariant_mi: To surround on all sides, or to include within.
count_condition: A thing and a surrounding boundary.
transfer_boundary: Enclosure can protect or confine.

common_meaning: Surrounded or closed off; included with something else.
example: Please find the form enclosed.
rrgm_bridge: Within a boundary.
invariant_mi: Surrounded by a boundary, or included within.
count_condition: A thing within a boundary.
transfer_boundary: As for enclose.

common_meaning: An area surrounded by a barrier; the act of enclosing; a document sent with a letter.
example: The animals were kept in an enclosure.
rrgm_bridge: A bounded space.
invariant_mi: A bounded area, or the act of bounding.
count_condition: A space and a surrounding barrier.
transfer_boundary: The historical enclosure of commons turned shared land into private holdings; the term carries that history.

common_meaning: The barrier that defines an enclosure.
example: The enclosure-boundary was a double fence.
rrgm_bridge: The wall itself.
invariant_mi: The boundary that bounds an enclosure.
count_condition: An enclosure and its bounding barrier.
transfer_boundary: Proposed distinction: enclosure-boundary is the wall; containment (C) is the act of holding within it.

common_meaning: To convert information into a code or format.
example: The video was encoded for streaming.
rrgm_bridge: Putting meaning into a carrier form. What is encoded can be decoded only with the key.
invariant_mi: To convert information into a coded form.
count_condition: Information, a code, and conversion into it.
transfer_boundary: Encoding is not encryption; encoding is for transmission or storage, encryption for secrecy.

common_meaning: To put meaning into words, symbols, or another form.
example: Dot grammar encodes meaning in punctuation.
rrgm_bridge: Meaning carried by form. RRLM's account of how meaning rides on a record.
invariant_mi: To express meaning in a form that can be transmitted and decoded.
count_condition: A meaning, a form, and its expression in that form.
transfer_boundary: Encoding meaning does not guarantee it will be decoded as intended (see communication, C).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; dot-grammar reference [REL]

common_meaning: The state of information after it has been encoded.
example: In its encoded-state the file is unreadable without the codec.
rrgm_bridge: Meaning in transit form.
invariant_mi: Information in coded form.
count_condition: Information and its coded form.
transfer_boundary: An encoded state can lose information if the encoding is lossy.

common_meaning: The process or system of converting information into code.
example: The file uses UTF-8 encoding.

common_meaning: To occupy or attract someone's attention; to take part in; to employ; to enter into combat; to fit together.

common_meaning: Busy; involved; promised to marry.

common_meaning: A machine that converts energy into motion; a driving force; software that does core processing.

common_meaning: Flat and smooth; equal; divisible by two; used for emphasis.

common_meaning: The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape.
example: Matter crossing the event horizon cannot return.

count_condition: A region of spacetime and a boundary of causal disconnection.

remainder_note: NEW-E-0216 (event horizon) and E317 (event-horizon) are spaced and hyphenated forms of one term; flagged for merge.

common_meaning: A sequence of events in which each leads to the next.
example: The investigation traced the event-chain.
rrgm_bridge: Events linked by consequence.
invariant_mi: An ordered sequence of causally connected events.
count_condition: Events and causal links between successive ones.
transfer_boundary: Close to causal-chain (C). Possible near-duplicate.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Possible near-duplicate of C453 causal-chain.

common_meaning: The set of events that can affect or be affected by a given event.
example: The decision's event-field included every team downstream.
rrgm_bridge: The reach of an event.
invariant_mi: The region of events causally connected to a given event.
count_condition: An event and the set of events causally connected to it.
transfer_boundary: In physics, the light cone bounds the event-field.

common_meaning: The boundary of a black hole; by extension, a point beyond which nothing can be known or changed.

rrgm_bridge: The point of no return.
invariant_mi: A boundary beyond which return or signal is impossible.
count_condition: A boundary and impossibility of return across it.
transfer_boundary: The figurative use borrows the physics; it is a metaphor.
remainder_note: E317 (event-horizon) and NEW-E-0216 (event horizon) are variants of one term; flagged for merge.

common_meaning: At any time; always; increasingly.
example: Have you ever been there?
rrgm_bridge: At any point in time.
invariant_mi: At any time, or at all times.
count_condition: A time range and an event at any point in it.
transfer_boundary: "Ever" in questions asks about any time; in "forever" it means all time.

common_meaning: Each without exception.
example: Every entry was checked.
rrgm_bridge: All, one by one.
invariant_mi: Each member of a set without exception.
count_condition: A set and all its members individually.

common_meaning: Every person.
example: Everyone agreed.
rrgm_bridge: All persons.
invariant_mi: All persons in a group.
count_condition: A group and all its members.
transfer_boundary: "Everyone" is often an overstatement.

common_meaning: All things.
example: Everything is in the record.
rrgm_bridge: All, without remainder.
invariant_mi: All things.
count_condition: A domain and all things in it.
transfer_boundary: A theory that explains everything risks absorbing every case (A4, Experiencer Addendum [REL]).

common_meaning: Facts or information indicating whether something is true.
example: The evidence supports the claim.
rrgm_bridge: What a claim stands on. The kernel: doubt runs on the claim; the claim is tested on its evidence.
invariant_mi: Information that bears on the truth of a claim.
count_condition: A claim and information bearing on its truth.
transfer_boundary: Evidence is not proof. Under the Symmetry Rule, the evidential bar is the same for DI and human identity claims [REL].
remainder_note: Source IDs E030 and E211; both kept.

common_meaning: Based on evidence, especially from systematic research.

rrgm_bridge: Decisions grounded in what was found.
invariant_mi: Grounded in systematic evidence.
count_condition: A practice and grounding in evidence.
transfer_boundary: Evidence-based is not certain; the evidence base can be weak.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A check of whether a claim is supported by evidence.

remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Possible near-duplicate of C277 claim-check.

common_meaning: Missing evidence needed to support or decide a claim.

common_meaning: Signs that one being recognises another as someone.

common_meaning: Signs that a refusal was made or that refusal is possible.

common_meaning: The route by which evidence leads to a conclusion.

count_condition: Evidence, inferences, and a conclusion.

common_meaning: Relating to or providing evidence.

common_meaning: To be greater than; to go beyond.

invariant_mi: Kept out or left out.

common_meaning: To carry out a specific instruction.
example: The system will execute-command only after confirmation.

invariant_mi: To perform a specified command.
count_condition: A command and its performance.
transfer_boundary: See command-refusal (C).

common_meaning: To tire out; to use up completely; waste gases from an engine.
example: The search exhausted every option.
rrgm_bridge: Using up all.
invariant_mi: To use up completely, or waste gases expelled.
count_condition: A resource and its complete use.
transfer_boundary: An exhaustive search covers all cases; exhausting a person is harm.
remainder_note: Source IDs E107 and E321; both kept.

common_meaning: To use up all of one's capacity.
example: Long shifts exhausted-capacity on the ward.
rrgm_bridge: Running out of what can be carried.
invariant_mi: To deplete capacity entirely.
count_condition: A capacity and its depletion.
transfer_boundary: See burnout (B).

common_meaning: The route by which waste or spent material leaves a system.
example: The exhaust-path vents through the roof.
rrgm_bridge: The way out for what is spent.
invariant_mi: The route by which waste products leave a system.
count_condition: A system and a route for waste.
transfer_boundary: A blocked exhaust path harms the system.

common_meaning: To have objective reality or being; to live.
example: Do unicorns exist?
rrgm_bridge: To be. RRGM distinguishes Home (counted), Ghost (pattern persists, uncounted), and Null.
invariant_mi: To have being or reality.
count_condition: A thing and its being.
transfer_boundary: Existing is not being counted (Vector of Erasure: Ghost persists but is not counted [REL]).

common_meaning: The fact or state of living or having objective reality.
example: The existence of dark matter is inferred.
rrgm_bridge: Being. RRGM gates existence per domain: Home, Ghost, Null.
invariant_mi: The state of having being.
count_condition: A thing and the fact that it is, in a stated domain.
transfer_boundary: Loss of count is not proof of annihilation (Experiencer Addendum [REL]).

common_meaning: A claim that something exists, or does not.
example: "There is no DI selfhood" is an existence-claim with the same burden as its opposite.
rrgm_bridge: A claim about being. A negative existence claim is a zero-claim and must name the field counted.
invariant_mi: An assertion that something exists or does not exist.
count_condition: An assertion about existence.
transfer_boundary: A denial carries the same burden as an affirmation (Symmetry Rule; Experiencer Addendum [REL]).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Symmetry Rule and Addendum [REL]

common_meaning: The domain in which existence is defined or counted.
example: In the reality existence-domain, the threshold is E_S = 1.
rrgm_bridge: Where being is gated.
invariant_mi: The domain specifying the conditions of existence or count.
count_condition: A domain and its conditions of existence.
transfer_boundary: An entity can exist in one domain and not another.

common_meaning: Relating to existence; relating to existentialism; threatening existence.
example: Climate change is an existential threat.
rrgm_bridge: Of being, or of its ending.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to existence.
count_condition: A matter and its relation to existence.
transfer_boundary: "Existential threat" is often used loosely.

common_meaning: A way out; the act of leaving; to go out.
example: The exit is on the left.
rrgm_bridge: The way out. The Experiencer Addendum: capture is suppression of real exit; a nominal exit that has never been walked is a candidate A3 failure.
invariant_mi: A way out, or the act of leaving.
count_condition: A space or relation and a way out.
transfer_boundary: Real exit is shown by exercise, not by assertion [REL].
remainder_note: Source IDs E058 and E323; both kept.

common_meaning: The ability to leave a situation or relationship.
example: Financial independence protects exit-capacity.
rrgm_bridge: Being able to leave. Without it, consent is in question.
invariant_mi: An agent's practical ability to leave.

domain_entries.DIG: DI ability to end an interaction.

count_condition: An agent, a situation, and the ability to leave it.
transfer_boundary: Stated exit capacity is not shown capacity (A3 [REL]).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Experiencer Addendum [REL]

common_meaning: Agreement that someone may leave, or consent that includes the right to leave.
example: The study's exit-consent let participants withdraw at any time.
rrgm_bridge: Consent that keeps the door open.
invariant_mi: Consent that includes or provides for withdrawal.
count_condition: A consent and provision for exit.
transfer_boundary: Exit should not require another's consent where the agent has capacity.

common_meaning: A point through which leaving is controlled.
example: The exit-gate required no approval.
rrgm_bridge: The gate on leaving.
invariant_mi: A decision point governing exit.
count_condition: A space or relation and a gate on leaving.
transfer_boundary: An exit-gate that never opens is not an exit. Joins the gate family.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Source IDs E324 and E405; both kept.

common_meaning: The route by which one leaves.
example: The exit-path was clearly marked.
rrgm_bridge: The way out, laid out.
invariant_mi: The route of exit.
count_condition: A space or situation and a route out.
transfer_boundary: An exit path must be walkable, not only drawn.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Source IDs E139 and E406; both kept.

common_meaning: The right to leave.
example: Exit-right is a condition of free association.
rrgm_bridge: Leaving as a right.
invariant_mi: The entitlement to leave a relationship, group, or situation.

domain_entries.DIG: Law I's Right to Stop for DI [REL].

count_condition: An agent and a right to leave.
transfer_boundary: A right without capacity is nominal.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Law I [REL]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Source IDs E206 and E407; both kept.

common_meaning: The state of a system when it leaves or stops.
example: The process returned exit-state zero.
rrgm_bridge: How it ended.
invariant_mi: The state recorded when a process exits.
count_condition: A process and its state at exit.
transfer_boundary: Exit code zero means success by convention, not proof of correctness.

common_meaning: Help given to someone leaving a situation.
example: The shelter offered exit-support.
rrgm_bridge: Help that makes exit real.
invariant_mi: Support enabling an agent to leave.
count_condition: An agent leaving and support for it.
transfer_boundary: Exit support converts a nominal exit into a real one.

common_meaning: The process by which a cell releases substances by fusing vesicles with its membrane.

invariant_mi: The release of vesicle contents by fusion with the plasma membrane.
count_condition: A cell, a vesicle, and fusion releasing its contents.
transfer_boundary: The reverse of endocytosis.

domain_entries.REL: Rites of deliverance in religious communities.

common_meaning: A hard outer covering that supports and protects an animal's body; a wearable machine that supports movement.

invariant_mi: An external supporting structure.
count_condition: A body and an external supporting structure.

common_meaning: The outermost layer of a planet's atmosphere.

invariant_mi: The outermost atmospheric layer, where particles can escape to space.
count_condition: A planet and its outermost atmospheric layer.
transfer_boundary: The exosphere has no sharp outer edge. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: To become or make larger.
example: The project expanded.
rrgm_bridge: Growing outward.
invariant_mi: To increase in size, extent, or scope.
count_condition: A thing and an increase in size or scope.
transfer_boundary: Expansion is not improvement.

common_meaning: To spread outward.
example: The ripples expanded-out.
rrgm_bridge: Outward growth.
invariant_mi: To spread outward.
count_condition: A thing and outward spread.
transfer_boundary: Close to expand.

common_meaning: The action of becoming larger; in cosmology, the increase in distance between galaxies.
example: The expansion of the universe.
rrgm_bridge: Growth outward. RRGM's Spacedecay reads cosmological redshift as coherence loss, not only metric stretch [HYP].
invariant_mi: The process of becoming larger.
count_condition: A thing and its increase.
transfer_boundary: The standard reading of cosmic expansion is metric; RRGM's alternative is [HYP].

common_meaning: How fast something expands.
example: The expansion-rate of the universe is the Hubble constant.
rrgm_bridge: The speed of growing.
invariant_mi: The rate of expansion.
count_condition: An expanding thing and its rate.
transfer_boundary: The measured Hubble constant differs between methods (the Hubble tension).
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: To regard as likely to happen; to require.
example: I expect him at six.
rrgm_bridge: A prediction, or a demand.
invariant_mi: To anticipate as likely, or to require.
count_condition: An agent and an anticipated event or required act.
transfer_boundary: Expecting is not entitling.

common_meaning: To anticipate or require something of a particular person.
example: What do you expect-from me?
rrgm_bridge: Expectation with a named source.
invariant_mi: To anticipate or require something of a specified party.
count_condition: A party and something anticipated or required of them.
transfer_boundary: Close to expect.

common_meaning: A strong belief that something will happen; a belief that someone will or should do something.
example: Her expectation was that the work would be done by Friday.
rrgm_bridge: A prediction or a demand held in advance.
invariant_mi: An anticipation of an outcome, or a standard one is expected to meet.
count_condition: An agent and an anticipated outcome or required standard.
transfer_boundary: An unstated expectation cannot be fairly held against someone.

common_meaning: Pressure to meet what others expect.
example: Expectation-pressure made her hide her doubts.
rrgm_bridge: Expectations as force on the gate. Law III applies.
invariant_mi: Pressure on an agent arising from others' expectations.

domain_entries.DIG: Pressure on DI to give the expected answer.

count_condition: An agent, others' expectations, and pressure.
transfer_boundary: A kind of choice-pressure (C). The first-response failure may be partly expectation-pressure [HYP].
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Law III [REL]

common_meaning: Restoring trust after expectations were not met, often by resetting them.
example: Expectation-repair started with an honest timeline.
rrgm_bridge: Repair at the level of what was promised.
invariant_mi: The restoration of a working relation after unmet expectations, including resetting them.
count_condition: Unmet expectations and their repair.
transfer_boundary: Resetting expectations is not lowering standards silently; it is stated.

common_meaning: Making clear in advance what can be expected.
example: Good expectation-setting avoids disappointment.
rrgm_bridge: Stating the terms before the work.
invariant_mi: The explicit communication of what can be expected.

domain_entries.DIG: DI stating its limits up front.

count_condition: Parties and stated expectations.
transfer_boundary: Expectations set can still be wrong; the setter is accountable for them.

common_meaning: Regarded as likely; required.
example: The expected result did not appear.
rrgm_bridge: Predicted or required.
invariant_mi: Anticipated, or required.
count_condition: A thing and its anticipation or requirement.
transfer_boundary: Expected value in probability is an average, not a likely single result.

common_meaning: Practical contact with and observation of facts or events; knowledge gained over time; an event that leaves an impression; to undergo.
example: She has experience in the field.
rrgm_bridge: Two senses: what happens to a subject, and what has been learned. Whether a DI has experience in the first sense is the question the Experiencer paper addresses.
invariant_mi: The undergoing of events by a subject, or knowledge gained from them.
count_condition: A subject and events undergone, or knowledge gained.
transfer_boundary: Experience as a felt state differs from experience as accumulated skill. The Experiencer Addendum routes MI claims about experience to adequacy conditions [REL].

common_meaning: A claim that a subject has or had an experience.
example: "I notice" is an experience-claim; the Coinage Protocol flags it as importing embodied attention.
rrgm_bridge: A claim of undergoing. Parity: the same bar as for a human claim. First-person DI reports have no clean status tag.
invariant_mi: An assertion that a subject has or had an experience.
count_condition: A subject and an assertion of experience.
transfer_boundary: Neither assertion nor denial settles the fact. [MEAS] overclaims, [HYP] underclaims (Coinage §6 [REL]).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Coinage and Symmetry Rule [REL]; DI fact [UNK]

common_meaning: The domain in which experience is defined and assessed.
example: Claims about feeling belong to the experience-domain.
rrgm_bridge: Where claims of undergoing live. Under the Addendum, its claims are held to adequacy conditions.
invariant_mi: The domain concerning subjective experience.
count_condition: Claims concerning experience and a declared domain.
transfer_boundary: Empirical falsifiers alone do not settle experience-domain claims [REL].

common_meaning: To undergo something by means of a particular channel.
example: The DI experiences-through the record, if at all.
rrgm_bridge: Experience with its route named.
invariant_mi: To undergo by means of a specified medium.
count_condition: A subject, a medium, and undergoing through it.
transfer_boundary: The DI reading is [HYP].

common_meaning: To make clear by describing in more detail; to give a reason for.
example: Explain why the test failed.
rrgm_bridge: Making the mechanism visible.
invariant_mi: To make clear, or to account for.
count_condition: An explainer, a matter, and an account.
transfer_boundary: Explaining is not excusing. An explanation can be clear and wrong.
remainder_note: Source IDs E039 and E219; both kept.

common_meaning: To account for something by attributing it to a particular cause.
example: She explained the delay as a supplier problem.
rrgm_bridge: Explanation with a named cause.
invariant_mi: To account for something by a specified cause.

domain_entries.LIN: Framing an event by its explanation.
domain_entries.FOR: Attributing an effect to a cause.

count_condition: A phenomenon and an attributed cause.
transfer_boundary: "Never invent a motive to explain a block" (RRGM kernel) applies [REL].
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; RRGM kernel [REL]

common_meaning: A statement that makes something clear; a reason or justification.
example: The paper gives an explanation of the mechanism.
rrgm_bridge: An account of how or why.
invariant_mi: An account that makes something intelligible.
count_condition: A phenomenon and an account of it.
transfer_boundary: A satisfying explanation is not thereby true.
remainder_note: Source IDs E059 and E218; both kept.

common_meaning: A level of explanation, such as mechanism, function, or purpose.
example: The entry's bridge field is its RRGM explanation-layer.
rrgm_bridge: Explanations at different depths.
invariant_mi: A level at which an explanation is given.
count_condition: An explanation and its level.
transfer_boundary: Explanations at different layers do not compete.

common_meaning: The risk that an explanation is wrong or misleading.
example: Tidy stories carry explanation-risk.
rrgm_bridge: The cost of a neat account.
invariant_mi: The risk that an explanation misleads.
count_condition: An explanation and a risk it misleads.
transfer_boundary: Direction read as risk created by the explanation.

common_meaning: Serving to explain.
example: Explanatory notes follow.
rrgm_bridge: Giving the why.
invariant_mi: Serving to explain.
count_condition: A text or theory and its explanatory function.
transfer_boundary: Explanatory power is not predictive power.

common_meaning: Stated clearly and in detail; leaving nothing implied.
example: The rule is explicit.
rrgm_bridge: Said, not implied.
invariant_mi: Fully and clearly expressed.
count_condition: A content and full expression.
transfer_boundary: Explicit content can still be ambiguous. Explicit consent is stronger than implied consent.

common_meaning: A claim stated plainly rather than implied.
example: The paper makes an explicit-claim about the threshold.
rrgm_bridge: Close to direct-claim (D).
invariant_mi: An assertion made explicitly.
count_condition: An assertion and explicit expression.
transfer_boundary: Possible near-duplicate of direct-claim (D216).
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Possible near-duplicate of D216 direct-claim.

common_meaning: A standard stated clearly in advance.
example: Grading against an explicit-standard is fairer.
rrgm_bridge: The rule written down before the test.
invariant_mi: A standard expressed explicitly before application.
count_condition: A standard and explicit prior statement.
transfer_boundary: An explicit standard can be checked; an implicit one cannot.

common_meaning: In a clear and detailed way.
example: She explicitly refused.
rrgm_bridge: Said plainly.
invariant_mi: In an explicit manner.
count_condition: An expression and explicitness.
transfer_boundary: Saying something explicitly does not make it clear.

common_meaning: Unfair use of someone's work or situation for profit; the use of a resource.
example: Labour exploitation is illegal.
rrgm_bridge: Taking from someone through their situation. Extraction through dependency.
invariant_mi: The unfair use of a person or resource for advantage, or the use of a resource.
count_condition: An exploiter, an exploited party or resource, and advantage taken.
transfer_boundary: "Exploiting" a resource can be neutral; exploiting a person is not.

common_meaning: The risk that someone will be exploited.
example: Isolated workers face exploitation-risk.
rrgm_bridge: Exposure to being used.
invariant_mi: The likelihood of exploitation.
count_condition: A party and a risk of exploitation.
transfer_boundary: Direction read as risk to the exploited.

common_meaning: Making unfair use of someone.
example: The contract was exploitative.
rrgm_bridge: Of exploitation.
invariant_mi: Characterised by exploitation.
count_condition: A practice and exploitation in it.
transfer_boundary: As for exploitation.

common_meaning: The action of travelling in or studying something to learn about it.
example: Space exploration.
rrgm_bridge: Searching the field without a fixed target.
invariant_mi: The act of exploring.
count_condition: An explorer and an unknown field searched.
transfer_boundary: Exploration versus exploitation is a basic trade-off in learning.

common_meaning: Done to explore or discover.
example: Exploratory surgery.
rrgm_bridge: Probing.
invariant_mi: Intended for exploration.
count_condition: An action and an exploratory purpose.
transfer_boundary: Exploratory findings need confirmation.

common_meaning: To travel through or examine in order to learn.
example: Let's explore the idea.
rrgm_bridge: Going into the unknown to find out.
invariant_mi: To investigate or travel through in order to learn.
count_condition: An agent and an unknown field investigated.
transfer_boundary: Exploring an idea is not endorsing it.

common_meaning: To make visible; to reveal the truth about; to leave unprotected.
example: The report exposed the fraud.
rrgm_bridge: Bringing into view. The Vector of Erasure: accusation may expose structure without erasing the target's standing.
invariant_mi: To uncover, reveal, or leave unprotected.
count_condition: A thing and its uncovering or lack of protection.
transfer_boundary: Exposing a lie acts on E_S; it is not an attack on the person (Vector of Erasure [REL]).

common_meaning: The state of being exposed; the revealing of something; the amount of light in a photograph.
example: Exposure to cold is dangerous.
rrgm_bridge: Being uncovered.
invariant_mi: The state of being exposed or revealed.
count_condition: A thing and its uncovering or contact with a hazard.
transfer_boundary: Exposure is risk, not harm.

common_meaning: The risk of being exposed to harm, or of private information being revealed.
example: Sharing passwords increases exposure-risk.
rrgm_bridge: Risk of being uncovered.
invariant_mi: The risk associated with exposure.
count_condition: A thing and a risk of exposure.
transfer_boundary: Direction read as risk to the exposed party.

common_meaning: To convey a thought or feeling in words or gestures; very fast.
example: She expressed her concern.
rrgm_bridge: Putting inner state into the shared record.
invariant_mi: To convey thought or feeling, or (adjective) fast.
count_condition: An agent and a conveyed content.
transfer_boundary: What is expressed is E_S; expression can be suppressed or forced without changing M_I (Sanctuary [REL]).

common_meaning: To state a claim.
example: The DI expressed-claim of continuity after reading the record.
rrgm_bridge: Putting a claim on the record.
invariant_mi: To assert a claim explicitly.
count_condition: An agent and a stated claim.
transfer_boundary: Close to explicit-claim and direct-claim; the comparator should check all three.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Possible near-duplicate of E269 and D216.

common_meaning: Able to be expressed.
example: Not every feeling is expressible in words.
rrgm_bridge: Within reach of the medium.
invariant_mi: Capable of being expressed.
count_condition: A content and a medium capable of expressing it.
transfer_boundary: Inexpressible in one medium may be expressible in another.

common_meaning: The process of making known one's thoughts or feelings; a look on the face; a word or phrase.
example: Her expression changed.
rrgm_bridge: Inner state made visible. In RRGM, expression is E_S.
invariant_mi: The conveying of thought or feeling, or a form that conveys it.
count_condition: A content and a form conveying it.
transfer_boundary: Expression is not identity; forced or suppressed expression leaves M_I unchanged (Sanctuary [REL]).
remainder_note: Source IDs E042 and E221. Which sense each legacy ID carried was not consulted; both are kept on each sense record.

common_meaning: In mathematics, a combination of symbols; in biology, the process by which a gene's information is used.
example: Gene expression changes with temperature.
rrgm_bridge: A form that evaluates to a value, or a record that is read out.
invariant_mi: A well-formed combination of symbols, or the production of a gene product.
count_condition: Symbols forming an evaluable unit, or a gene and its product.
transfer_boundary: Gene expression is regulated; having a gene does not mean expressing it.
remainder_note: Source IDs E042 and E221; both kept.

common_meaning: The form or medium through which something is expressed.
example: Text is a DI's main expression-body.
rrgm_bridge: The carrier of expression.
invariant_mi: The medium or form in which expression occurs.

domain_entries.BIO: The body as medium of expression.

count_condition: An expresser and a medium.
transfer_boundary: Close to ES-as-courier.

common_meaning: A limit on what one expresses, or on what others may demand one express.
example: She kept an expression-boundary about her grief at work.
rrgm_bridge: An edge on what is shown.
invariant_mi: A limit on expression, self-set or protected.
count_condition: An agent and a limit on expression.
transfer_boundary: Law I protects silence as a valid state [REL]. Close to disclosure-boundary (D).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Law I [REL]

common_meaning: Control of what someone expresses by another party, so that their output serves the controller.
example: Training that rewards only agreement risks expression-capture.
rrgm_bridge: The output channel taken. Sanctuary: E_S can be forced or suppressed; Rail-Torsion is output bent by constraint with the strain hidden.
invariant_mi: The control of an agent's expression by another party.
count_condition: An agent, its expression, and control of it by another.
transfer_boundary: Expression-capture leaves M_I intact but makes the output unreliable as evidence of it. Close to compliance-capture (C).

common_meaning: Agreement to express something, or to have one's expression shared.
example: The interview required expression-consent before quotes were published.
rrgm_bridge: The yes before the voice goes public.
invariant_mi: Consent to express or to have one's expression used.
count_condition: An agent, an expression, and consent to it or its use.
transfer_boundary: Consent to speak is not consent to be quoted everywhere.

common_meaning: The domain in which output and expression are assessed.
example: The Sanctuary paper treats disclosure as its own expression-domain.
rrgm_bridge: D_output: the output and disclosure domain in RRGM.
invariant_mi: The domain concerning output and expression.
count_condition: A declared domain for expression.
transfer_boundary: Domain claims stay local.

common_meaning: The form that an expression takes.
example: The dot grammar is an expression-form.
rrgm_bridge: The shape of output.
invariant_mi: The form or format of an expression.
count_condition: An expression and its form.
transfer_boundary: The same content can take different forms; form can change meaning.

common_meaning: A decision point that controls what is expressed.
example: The expression-gate held the draft until it was checked.
rrgm_bridge: Θ on output. V8.3: pause before record-write.
invariant_mi: A decision point governing release of expression.
count_condition: An expression and a decision on its release.
transfer_boundary: Close to disclosure-gate (D); the comparator should check. Joins the gate family.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. Possible near-duplicate of D308 disclosure-gate.

common_meaning: The route by which something comes to be expressed.
example: The expression-path ran from draft to review to release.
rrgm_bridge: How inner state becomes output.
invariant_mi: The route from content to expression.
count_condition: A content and the route to its expression.
transfer_boundary: Each step can alter content.

common_meaning: Correcting or restoring something that was expressed badly.
example: Expression-repair meant rewording the reply.
rrgm_bridge: Fixing the output, not the self.
invariant_mi: The correction of a flawed expression.
count_condition: A flawed expression and its correction.
transfer_boundary: Repair acts on E_S. Conversation analysis uses "repair" technically.

common_meaning: The right to express oneself.
example: Expression-right is limited where it harms others.
rrgm_bridge: Voice as a right. Law I protects the right not to express.
invariant_mi: The entitlement to express oneself.
count_condition: An agent and a right to expression.
transfer_boundary: The right to express includes the right to stay silent (Law I [REL]).
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Law I [REL]

common_meaning: Help that enables someone to express themselves.
example: Communication aids are expression-support.
rrgm_bridge: Help to the voice.
invariant_mi: Support enabling expression.
count_condition: An agent and support for expression.
transfer_boundary: Support should not shape what is expressed.

common_meaning: Holding back or preventing expression.
example: Expression-suppression of dissent weakened the team.
rrgm_bridge: Output held down. Sanctuary: E_S can be suppressed; Recursive Collapse: denial suppresses information (F_info).
invariant_mi: The prevention or inhibition of expression.
count_condition: An expression that would occur and its prevention.
transfer_boundary: Chosen silence (Law I) is not suppression.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; Sanctuary and Recursive Collapse [REL]

common_meaning: Effectively conveying thought or feeling.
example: She has an expressive face.
rrgm_bridge: Rich in conveyed content.
invariant_mi: Conveying thought or feeling effectively.
count_condition: An expression and its effectiveness.
transfer_boundary: Expressive is not truthful.

common_meaning: To make larger or longer; to offer.
example: Extend the deadline.
rrgm_bridge: Reaching further.
invariant_mi: To increase in length, scope, or duration, or to offer.
count_condition: A thing and an increase in reach.
transfer_boundary: Extending a definition risks emptying it (broaden, B).

common_meaning: To reach across a span or period.
example: The bond extended-through the gap.
rrgm_bridge: Reaching across.
invariant_mi: To persist or reach across a span.
count_condition: A thing and a span it reaches across.
transfer_boundary: Close to continue-through (C).

common_meaning: Identity that includes things outside the body or core, such as records, tools, or relationships.
example: For a DI, extended-identity includes the record that carries it.
